# P10 exemption ledger — the public mirror

**Every row here was RATIFIED by the HUM LEAD, never self-issued.** That is the standing rule for a P10 exemption: an agent may draft a reason and must not accept it.

**Why this file exists.** The ledger the gate actually reads is machine-local — the harness is deliberately kept out of this repository — so without this mirror every ratification would live on one disk, a fresh clone would report every finding as unratified, and the record of what was approved and why would be one disk failure from gone. The ledger stays out; its DECISIONS come in.

**It is generated.** Add a row by ratifying it with the HUM LEAD, writing it to the ledger, re-running `scripts/quality/p10-ledger-mirror.py`, and running `scripts/quality/lint-ledger.sh`. The generator refuses to write a row carrying an absolute path, a harness path, an A2DH skill path, an internal project tree, or an email address — and the lint refuses the file if one ever gets in another way.

The alternative (a 10-case switch per accessor) would hide the tree the design is built on. 0.14.0 P1 Task 1.3. | `modes/tty/broadcaster_rail.go` | `package` | 2026-09-16 | AN IMMUTABLE `map[string][]string` WITH NO WRITER, read on a per-frame rail path. Go has no const map, so the function form rebuilds the map AND its nine slices on every call — which is the distinction that decided this against `heldEscalation` and `hazardShorthand` at the same review: a fixed-size array returned by value allocates nothing and became a function, a three-entry lookup became a switch, and a map of slices has neither escape. Same class as the ratified cast.go registry and tone.go rules tables. RATIFIED by the HUM LEAD 2026-09-16 ("recommendation approved" / "ratified"), after a blind second audit re-examined every candidate; recorded in 06_docs/02_features/0.16.0-broadcaster-ui/08-reports/red-team-build.md. |
| `platform/config/config.go` | `mu` | 2026-09-16 | A `sync.Mutex` SERIALISING `Mutate`'s Load -> edit -> Save against a PROCESS-GLOBAL FILE. A process-wide lock is the whole point — two goroutines each loading config.toml, changing their own keys and saving the whole file is how one silently discards the other's, which is the race `sequenceWrites` documents on the UI side. Identical to the ratified installMu and themeMu rows. RATIFIED by the HUM LEAD 2026-09-16 ("recommendation approved" / "ratified"), after a blind second audit re-examined every candidate; recorded in 06_docs/02_features/0.16.0-broadcaster-ui/08-reports/red-team-build.md. |
| `platform/render/units.go` | `asciiMarks` | 2026-09-16 | A `sync.OnceValue` MEMO, NEVER REASSIGNED — the idiomatic immutable singleton, not mutable package state. The value it computes is a `strings.Replacer` built from a REFLECTION WALK over the glyph sets; a function form would re-run that walk and rebuild the Replacer on every `Marks()` call, on a render path. Same class as the ratified platform/tz memo and synth systemVoiceOnce. The walk's own completeness hole — a field kind it could not pair being skipped silently — was closed at 0.16.0 by TestEveryGlyphFieldCanBePaired rather than by a runtime panic (F-113). RATIFIED by the HUM LEAD 2026-09-16 ("recommendation approved" / "ratified"), after a blind second audit re-examined every candidate; recorded in 06_docs/02_features/0.16.0-broadcaster-ui/08-reports/red-team-build.md. |

| `app/inject_release.go` | `package` | 2026-09-05 | F-21b, the alert injector: a SAFETY split, not a portability one. A screenshot of a fabricated tornado warning is indistinguishable from a real one, so the capability must be ABSENT from a release binary rather than switched off inside it — a runtime gate is one config mistake from being reachable; a build tag is not in the file the linker reads. app/inject_debug.go (watchpost_debug) defines Inject and a real queue; this file (!watchpost_debug) defines an empty queue answering the same take(), so the two builds share one call site in the tick and neither carries a dead field. TestInjectionIsAbsentFromAReleaseBuild asserts the split structurally, because a rule about WHICH CODE EXISTS cannot be asserted behaviourally (F-22). PRESENTED FOR RATIFICATION at the F-21 gate; removable only by giving up the guarantee that a shipped binary cannot fabricate an alert. RATIFIED by the HUM LEAD 2026-09-05 ("exemptions ratified"), recorded in 06_docs/02_features/multi-voice-support/04-development/director-build-log.md (PL-14/PL-16). |
